name: Ardalan Kahak
title: R&D Engineer, Research Scientist, Mechanical Engineer.
tagline: I design, fabricate, and validate electromechanical prototypes — soft robotics, wearable sensors, and programmable interfaces — from concept through working prototype.
about: Mechanical Engineering Ph.D. candidate at Virginia Tech specializing in electromechanical system design, soft robotics, and prototype development. My work spans programmable acoustic holograms, inflatable Kirigami interfaces, soft piezoelectric  reservoir-computing patches, and haptic interfaces, with hands-on experience in embedded electronics, sensor integration, fabrication, and control systems. I also bring industry experience in large-scale automation and manufacturing. I am seeking advanced R&D, soft robotics, or wearable electronics roles where cross-disciplinary engineering and hands-on fabrication can drive innovative product development.

experience.summary: Fabricating and validating soft electromechanical prototypes with integrated sensors for acoustics, haptics, soft robotics, and physical reservoir computing.
bullets: Fabricated prototypes and mechanical assemblies with integrated sensors using layer-by-layer fabrication and geometry-driven design principles
Designed, built, and validated a low-power underwater physical reservoir computing sensor combining embedded sensors, piezoelectric materials, and DAQ systems with mechanical design optimization
Developed an inflatable compliant Kirigami interface with embedded sensors for closed-loop feedback control of exoskeleton comfort, using a single pneumatic input for actuation and force regulation

Coordinated with external vendors and led post-installation troubleshooting to improve system performance and reliability
